raw_case_text:
A 13-year-old boy was referred to our hospital with complaints of high-grade fever, non-bilious, non-bloody projectile vomiting, light headedness, generalized weakness, reduced appetite and passing black-coloured urine. Prior to his admission, the child was febrile (40  C) with blood pressure of 110/40 mmHg (considered to be low as per guidelines of the National Institute of Health), along with thrombocytopaenia (28 000 mm-3 blood; normal: 1.5-4.5 mm-3 blood), low haematological parameters of haemoglobin (12.3 g dl-1; normal: 10-15.5 g dl-1), haematocrit (35.8 %; normal: 35-44 %), mean corpuscular volume (66.1 fl; normal: 80-95 fl) and mean corpuscular haemoglobin (22.7 pg; normal: 32-36 pg). Blood urea (62 mg dl-1; normal: 5-18 mg dl-1) and random blood sugar (204 mg dl-1; normal: 70-140 mg dl-1) levels were significantly raised. Peripheral blood smear examination was positive for P. vivax. Other tests such as Dengue (Non-structural protein 1) NS1, scrub typhus card tests, Widal test and COVID 19 reverse transcriptase (RT)-PCR were negative. Despite thrombocytopaenia, the child had no bleeding manifestations and was administered a first dose of intravenous artesunate and intravenous fluids.
With the impending hypovolaemia, and persistent hypotension with an episode of loss of consciousness for 20 min, the child was referred to our hospital. He was afebrile, hypotensive (88/36 mmHg), with high pulse rate (110 bpm) and facial swelling. There was reduction in urine output of around 150 ml per day, but the oxygen saturation (SpO2) was well maintained. Liver was enlarged up to 2 cm below the right costal margin. Other systemic examinations were within normal limits. Upon laboratory investigations, his haemoglobin level was 11 g dl-1, with a low haematocrit (34.2 %), mean corpuscular volume (71 fl) and mean corpuscular haemoglobin (22.9 pg) values with platelet count of 36 000 mm-3 blood. Serum direct bilirubin and liver enzymes were elevated. Giemsa-stained peripheral blood smears revealed normal sized erythrocytes with microgametocytes containing malarial pigments (Fig. 1). Quantitative buffy coat (QBC) examination detected gametocytes of non-falciparum species. Blood sample was subjected to a multiplex nested PCR assay using published primers (Table 1), and an amplified product of 121 bp corresponding with P. vivax was detected by 1.5 % agarose gel electrophoresis using a molecular ladder of 100 bp (Thermo Scientific Gene Ruler 100 bp ladder) (Fig. 2). Buffer used for the agarose gel cast and running buffer in the gel electrophoresis tank was 10x Tris boric acid EDTA (TBE). The child was treated with injectable inotropes, intravenous fluids, oxygenation, the remaining two doses of artesunate and injectable antibiotics (ceftriaxone and vancomycin). Antibiotics were discontinued after malaria was reported. A repeat complete haemogram showed a fall of platelets to 19 000 mm-3 blood after 7 h of treatment, but the child became stable after 22 h with the same regimen and was discharged with advice to continue artemether-lumefantrine combination without any other drugs and/or antibiotics.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 13-year-old boy presenting with high-grade fever, projectile vomiting, lightheadedness, weakness, and passage of black-colored urine.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 13-year-old boy presented with high-grade fever, projectile non-bilious non-bloody vomiting, lightheadedness, generalized asthenia, anorexia, and passing black-colored urine. At a primary healthcare facility, he was documented to have high fever (40 C), hypotension (110/40 mmHg), and severe thrombocytopenia. Following initial resuscitation and antipyresis, he developed persistent refractory hypotension, impending hypovolemic shock, and an episode of loss of consciousness lasting 20 minutes, prompting urgent referral to a tertiary hospital.
subjective.past_medical_history: No documented chronic illnesses. Pre-admission administration of one dose of intravenous artesunate and intravenous fluids at referring center.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for high fever, projectile non-bloody non-bilious vomiting, lightheadedness, generalized weakness, anorexia, dark black urine, facial swelling, and transient syncope. Negative for active mucosal or cutaneous bleeding manifestations. Allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Afebrile, hypotensive with blood pressure 88/36 mmHg, pulse rate 110 beats/min, SpO2 well maintained on room air. Facial swelling present. Urine output markedly reduced to approximately 150 mL/day (oliguria). Abdominal examination revealed tender hepatomegaly palpable 2 cm below the right costal margin. Other systemic examinations were unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Pre-referral laboratory tests: hemoglobin 12.3 g/dL, hematocrit 35.8%, MCV 66.1 fL, MCH 22.7 pg, platelet count 28,000/mm3, blood urea 62 mg/dL, random blood sugar 204 mg/dL. Tertiary admission laboratory tests: hemoglobin 11 g/dL, hematocrit 34.2%, MCV 71 fL, MCH 22.9 pg, platelet count 36,000/mm3 (declining to 19,000/mm3 at 7 hours post-treatment), elevated direct bilirubin, and elevated transaminases. Negative investigations: Dengue NS1 antigen, scrub typhus card test, Widal agglutination test, and SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR. Peripheral blood smears and quantitative buffy coat (QBC) performed.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Severe Plasmodium vivax malaria complicated by blackwater fever (intravascular hemolysis with hemoglobinuria), severe thrombocytopenia, oliguric acute renal failure, and impending hypovolemic/septic shock.
Diagnostic confirmation: Giemsa-stained peripheral blood smear demonstrating microgametocytes containing malarial pigments; QBC detecting non-falciparum gametocytes; multiplex nested PCR confirming a 121-bp amplicon specific for Plasmodium vivax. Dengue NS1, scrub typhus, Widal, and COVID-19 tests were negative.
Treatment & Outcome: Managed with intravenous fluid resuscitation, injectable inotropic support, oxygenation, completed remaining two doses of intravenous artesunate, and empiric IV ceftriaxone and vancomycin (discontinued once diagnosis confirmed). Thrombocytopenia nadired at 19,000/mm3 at 7 hours, followed by hemodynamic stabilization, recovery of urine output by 22 hours, and discharge on oral artemether-lumefantrine combination therapy with complete recovery.
